transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The U.S.'s big employment report is out.
Businesses added 29,000 jobs last month,
far below what economists projected.
But Gus Fouche, the chief economist for PNC Financial Services Group,
seems upbeat about the fact that the unemployment rate rose slightly to 4.2%.
The reason it rose is because we had more people looking for work over the month.
That's actually a good sign.
We've seen fewer people looking for work in recent months,
in part because of restrictions on immigration.
But if we see more people entering the labor force, more people looking for work,
that means they're encouraged by the job market.
Gains in wages, an important measure of the job market strength,
have not kept pace with rising prices in recent months.
The overall economy is a dominant issue ahead of the November midterm elections.
But President Trump heads to Alabama today for a campaign rally.
He had vowed to help Republicans in the most competitive midterm races.
Instead, he's hitting reliably red states.
Yesterday in Durant, Oklahoma,
thousands of people waited hours in the rain to see Trump.
From Member Station KOSU, Sierra Fiverr reports.
Throngs of people from across Oklahoma and Texas
snaked outside the Choctaw Nation event center
hours before Trump was scheduled to appear.
Despite sagging approval ratings, those who made the trip still back him.
That includes Mona Atkinson, who traveled down from Seminole to see the president.
She says she wants to support the people Trump is endorsing.
When he puts his staff of approval on these candidates,
we believe that they will legitimately toe the line for our party,
for our conservative values, for our Christian values.
A handful of Republican candidates attended the event,
hoping Trump's blessing will translate into victory in November.
For NPR News, I'm Sierra Fiverr in Durant.
The fly Dubai pilots in an altercation this week
that forced an emergency landing of their plane
are now in the United Arab Emirates.
Most of the passengers who are on the plane are Israeli.
The UAE is investigating the case and potential motives.
NPR's Abit Rawi has more from Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia says the pilots left the city of Tabuk on Thursday
and were flown to the United Arab Emirates
accompanied by an Emirati security team.
Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says the plane's captain
was stabbed by his co-pilot before Israeli passengers
entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker.
In a video call with India's prime minister,
the Indian captain of the plane tells him from a hospital bed in the UAE
that he managed to open the cockpit door while being attacked.
The plane made an emergency landing Wednesday morning in Tabuk,
where both pilots were hospitalized for injuries.
Netanyahu says the pilot who attacked the plane's captain is from Oman.
This has yet to be confirmed by Emirati Saudi or Omani authorities.
Aya Bhatrawi, NPR News, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
This is NPR News.
Thousands of people protested in the Indian city of Mumbai
against what they say is a systemic effort by the government
to disenfranchise voters unlikely to favor the ruling Hindu
Nationalist Party.
We have this from NPR's Adia Hadid.
Crowds chant, "Where does the vote theft happen?"
in the office of the BJP.
That's the party led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The protests were called by student-led political movement
after a local daily, the Indian Express,
reported that some 130 million people were struck off revised voter rolls
and that senior election commissioners repeatedly complained
over what they saw as illegal or unwarranted actions
during the campaign to revise voter lists.
One protester who requested anonymity over fears of retribution
said she believes the voter revisions were conducted
to help the Prime Minister's party.
You're going to take away someone's vote.
That's basically the only thing we have.
The election commission has denied the allegations.
Adia Hadid, NPR News, Mumbai.
the building. You're listening to NPR News.

topics.text: U.S. businesses added 29,000 jobs last month, far below economist projections; unemployment rate rises to 4.2%
President Trump campaigns in Durant, Oklahoma despite vowing to help in competitive races; thousands attend rally
Fly Dubai pilots involved in altercation forcing emergency landing are now in United Arab Emirates
Israeli captain stabbed by co-pilot on Fly Dubai flight; plane made emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia
Thousands protest in Mumbai against alleged government effort to disenfranchise voters opposed to ruling Hindu Nationalist Party
